Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are working in the Moneo repo (read AGENTS.md first and follow it: tests, privacy, QA backend, commits). Goal: chat attachments work for every document type on every AI source, and answers cite where they came from.

Current state (commit 9e7e5aee on main): `lib/ai/chat-attachments.ts` allows only jpg/png/webp/pdf, 4 MB max (an old serverless limit that no longer applies; Moneo runs locally). `app/api/chat/attachments/route.ts` stores files in the private "chat" storage bucket. `app/api/chat/route.ts` (~line 145) sends the current message's files to the model as raw `file` parts. Only on the Claude source (`lib/ai/claude.ts` ~line 184) is a PDF turned into text with `lib/ai/pdf-text.ts` (unpdf). The ChatGPT sign-in source (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`) and API key providers (see `lib/ai/provider.ts`, `lib/ai/keys.ts`) may not handle PDF file parts. Earlier messages' files show up only as names (`attachmentNote`).

Decisions made by the owner (do not change them):
1. Supported types: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX (also XLS if cheap), CSV/TSV, plus photos (jpg/png/webp). Raise the size limit to something sensible for local use (e.g. 25 MB) and keep the per-message count limit. Sniff the real type from bytes, as now (DOCX/PPTX/XLSX are zip files; check the inner content types). Update the upload UI's accept list and the error copy.
2. Every document becomes text on the owner's computer, the same way for every AI source, with location markers: "Page n" for PDF, "Slide n" (including speaker notes) for PPTX, headings and paragraph numbers for DOCX, sheet name plus A1 cell/row references for XLSX/CSV (tables in a compact form; cut large sheets with a clear note, and let the tool below page through the rest). Photos stay image parts for every source. Use existing deps first (`exceljs` and `papaparse` are already in package.json, `unpdf` for PDF). Add a small, well-maintained dependency for DOCX/PPTX only if needed (a zip reader plus XML parsing is fine).
3. Scanned PDFs, or PDF pages with no text layer: render those pages to images on the computer and send them to the model as image parts (cap the number of pages, say so when cut). Drop the old "ask for photos" path.
4. Add a chat tool `document_read` (read-only) that lets the model reopen any file attached earlier in the same conversation, by name/id plus a page/slide/sheet/cell range or a text search. Earlier files are then listed with their ids in the history note instead of only their names. Cache the extracted text if it's cheap (e.g. keyed by storage path), but don't add a migration unless it's clearly needed.
5. Citations as inline chips: when the model uses a document, it cites with a compact marker right after the sentence, which the chat renders as a small clickable chip such as `statement.pdf · p.3` or `budget.xlsx · Sheet1!B12`. Clicking opens the file (through the existing GET attachments route) at that location: PDF via `#page=n`; for other types open an in-app viewer/sheet showing the extracted section with the quoted text highlighted where possible. Pick a marker syntax that is easy for models to write and safe to parse (validate it with Zod, show only chips that point to files in this conversation). Add one short citation rule to SYSTEM_PROMPT in `lib/ai/provider.ts`. Keep your prompt edit to that one paragraph: another agent is rewriting the rest of the prompt in parallel. Render chips in `components/ai-message.tsx` (check how `moneo-chart` blocks are rendered and stripped from history in `app/api/chat/route.ts` ~line 41).
6. It must work on all sources: API key providers (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic API, etc.), ChatGPT sign-in, and Claude sign-in. Remove the Claude-only PDF path in claude.ts once the shared path covers it.

Check every surface listed in AGENTS.md ("Hit every surface"): phone layout, light/dark, the voice call if it accepts attachments, history reload. Tests: unit tests for the type sniffing and the extraction of each format, with tiny generated fixtures (no personal data), and for citation parsing. A Playwright journey only if no existing chat spec can take it. Verify against the QA backend/server (`npm run qa:server`), never the owner's. Real AI calls cost money; mock them in tests. One quick manual real check against the dev AI key is okay if one is configured in `.env.qa`.

When done: run npm test, lint, typecheck and build. Commit in steps on your branch, push, and open a PR against main (you may open it without asking; never merge it). End the PR body with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)" and commits with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Report back the PR URL and any decisions you made yourself.

Moneo can run on your Claude subscription instead of an API key. It uses Claude Code, which comes with Moneo, signed in with your own Claude account on this computer. Moneo never sees or stores your Claude login; Claude Code keeps it, the same one the Claude Code app uses.

1. In **Settings → AI access**, click **Sign in with Claude** on this computer. A Claude sign-in page opens in your browser.

## Everyday use

- **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running).
- **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it.
- **Update Moneo:**
  ```sh
  git pull
  npm ci
  npm run setup
  npm run build
  npm start
  ```
  Your data and secrets are kept.

While Moneo runs it does its background work by itself: scheduled summaries, and syncing your bank and Scalable about once a day. Anything missed while your computer was off runs shortly after you start Moneo.

Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. A short message in the corner of Home tells you once about old values and about a connection that failed or needs reconnecting.

## Good to know

- Moneo only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so other devices on your network can't open it unless you turn on [phone and tablet access](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional).
- Your data lives in the Docker volumes `moneo_db-data` and `moneo_storage-data`. `docker compose down` keeps them; **`docker compose down -v` deletes all your data**.
- If ports 54321 or 54322 are already in use, add `API_PORT=` and `DB_PORT=` with free ports to `.env` and run `npm run setup` again.

**One shared path for every AI source** (`lib/ai/documents/`): each document becomes text on the owner's computer with locations, and that text is what API-key providers, ChatGPT sign-in and Claude sign-in all receive. Photos stay image parts.
- PDF: `--- Page n ---` per page (unpdf). Pages with no text layer are rendered to JPEG with `@napi-rs/canvas` and sent as images, at most 10 per message, with a note naming any pages left out. The old "ask for photos" path is gone.
- PPTX: `--- Slide n ---` in presentation order, with speaker notes (slide-number fields dropped).
- DOCX: `[¶n]` paragraph numbers, `#` headings by style (including localized style ids), table rows as `| a | b |`, deleted text in tracked changes skipped.
- XLSX/CSV: compact tables with a column-letter header and row numbers (`=== Sheet "Budget" (A1:C4) ===`). Dates come out as ISO dates and formulas as their results. CSV handles `;` and tabs, and Windows-1252 exports.
- Long documents are cut at a unit boundary with a note naming the next range. Text is split evenly across a message's documents (about 150k characters in total).

**`document_read` tool** (read-only): reopens any file attached in the conversation by its id (or exact name), using a location (`p.3-5`, `slide.2`, `para.10-40`, `Sheet1!A1:F200`) or a text search that returns locations. Earlier files are now listed as `name (id a1b2c3d4)` in the history note. Extracted text is cached in memory by storage path (LRU, 24 files; files never change). No migration.

**Citations**: the model writes `{{cite ID LOCATION "optional quote"}}` right after a sentence (one paragraph added to `SYSTEM_PROMPT`). `AiMessage` turns valid markers that point to files in this conversation into chips such as `statement.pdf · p.3` and drops the rest (and any marker still being streamed). PDFs and photos open through the existing GET route (`#page=n` for PDFs). DOCX, PPTX and sheet chips open a sheet-style viewer that shows the cited paragraphs, slide or cells with the quote or cell highlighted, using the new `GET /api/chat/attachments/section`. The Claude-only PDF path (`lib/ai/pdf-text.ts`, `readPdfs` in `claude.ts`) is removed.

## Decisions I made
- **XLS (old binary Excel) is not supported.** exceljs can't read it, and supporting it would mean adding SheetJS (not on npm's registry) or an OLE2 parser. Not cheap.
- **New dependencies:** `@napi-rs/canvas` 1.0.11 (unpdf's documented renderer for Node, prebuilt binaries, added to `serverExternalPackages`) and `jszip`. jszip was already installed through exceljs; it is now listed directly. DOCX/PPTX XML is read with a small tokenizer, with no XML library.
- A PDF page counts as "no text layer" when it has fewer than 10 non-space characters.
- Ids are the first 8 hex characters of the file's random storage name. Chips resolve against the attachments of the messages loaded in the chat, so a citation to a file on an older, unloaded page of a very long chat shows no chip.

PR #210 is open (not merged): chat attachments now work for every document type on every AI source, and answers cite where facts came from with small clickable chips. One gap: no real AI call was made, because `.env.qa` has no AI key. The model side is covered only by stubbed replies and unit tests.

**Checks:**
- `npm test`: everything passes except one run where `supabase/tests/migration-replay.test.ts` timed out under load. It passes on its own, and I didn't touch migrations.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm run check:bundle` pass.
- The new browser journey `e2e/chat-attachments.gated.spec.ts` passes against the QA backend. It uploads a generated XLSX, stubs a reply with one valid and one foreign citation, and opens the valid chip on its highlighted cell.
- I looked at phone and desktop screenshots in light and dark. That caught long file names hiding the location on chips, which I fixed: the name is cut, the location always shows.
- Ports 3100 and 3101 were taken by other sessions' servers, which I left alone. I ran this checkout's QA server on 3137 and stopped it afterwards.

**What changed:**
- **Types and limits:** PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV/TSV and photos, up to 25 MB each, still 4 per message. Types are sniffed from the bytes. The upload hint, accept list and error messages are updated.
- **Shared extraction:** every document becomes text on the computer, the same for all sources, with pages, slides, numbered paragraphs, or sheets with row numbers and column letters. PDF pages with no text are drawn as JPEG images, at most 10 per message, with a note naming any skipped pages. The old "ask for photos" path and the Claude-only PDF code are gone.
- **`document_read`:** a read-only tool that reopens any earlier file in the conversation by id, with a location range or a text search. Earlier files now appear with their ids in the history note. Extracted text is cached in memory by storage path, so there's no migration.
- **Citations:** the model writes `{{cite ID LOCATION "quote"}}`. The chat shows chips only for files in this conversation and drops the rest. PDFs open at the page (`#page=n`). Word, PowerPoint and spreadsheet chips open a viewer showing that part of the file with the quote or cell highlighted. Voice calls leave the markers out of what they say.
- **Prompt:** I added one paragraph on citations to `SYSTEM_PROMPT` and touched nothing else in it.
- **Also updated:** `README.md`, the app guide and tool-progress labels.

**Decisions I made:**
- **No XLS (old binary Excel):** `exceljs` can't read it, and support would need a heavy extra parser.
- **New dependency `@napi-rs/canvas` 1.0.11:** it renders scanned PDF pages, and is the renderer `unpdf` documents for Node. It's a native package with prebuilt binaries.
- **`jszip` is now a direct dependency:** it was already installed through `exceljs`. DOCX and PPTX are read with a small XML tokenizer, no XML library.
- **Larger request limit:** I set `proxyClientMaxBodySize: "26mb"`, because the proxy only buffers 10 MB by default, which would break 25 MB uploads.
- **Scan threshold:** a PDF page counts as a scan when it has fewer than 10 non-space characters.
- **File ids:** each id is the first 8 hex characters of the file's random storage name.
- **Known limits:**
  - In a very long chat, a citation to a file on an older page that isn't loaded shows no chip.
  - `document_read` can't reopen photos.
  - UTF-16 CSV files are refused.
- No AGENTS.md change needed.
